9 Using packdir as a library

9.1 From Rust

Add packdir as a dependency. Features choose the engines.

[dependencies]
packdir = { git = "https://github.com/querygraph/packdir" }
# or, without Turso:
# packdir = { git = "https://github.com/querygraph/packdir", default-features = false, features = ["sqlite"] }

Open a container, bring it up to date with a directory, and read a member:

use packdir::container::{Apply, Container, OpenOptions};
use packdir::tursolite::{Engine, Journal};

let options = OpenOptions {
    engine: Some(Engine::Turso),
    journal: Journal::Mvcc,
    ..OpenOptions::default()
};
let c = Container::open("leaf.sqlar".as_ref(), &options)?;
let apply = Apply { writers: 4, ..Apply::default() };
let (stored, retained, bytes) = c.update(apply, &[], "plain/leaf")?;
let data = c.read("a_320")?;
assert!(c.verify()?.is_empty());
c.close()?; // seals what Turso wrote

Call close. A container dropped without it is left as after a crash, for the next open to recover.

The crate also exports container::repack, container::plan, container::barrier, cli::pack_tree for a whole tree, and tursolite, the database layer.

9.2 From OCaml and OxCaml

let c = Packdir.Container.open_ ~engine:Tursolite.Turso ~journal:Packdir.Container.Mvcc "leaf.sqlar" in
let stored, retained, bytes = Packdir.Container.update ~writers:4 c "plain/leaf" in
let data = Packdir.Container.read c "a_320" in
assert (Packdir.Container.verify c = []);
Packdir.Container.close c

Packdir.Container is the format, Packdir.Fileutils the file commands, Packdir.Cli the whole command line, and Packdir.Native the SHA-256, nanosecond stat, utimensat and F_FULLFSYNC calls.

9.3 firstpair-tursolite

The database layer is its own package, because it has nothing to do with archives. It offers one interface over SQLite and Turso, with the same shape in Rust and in OCaml:

Rust OCaml and OxCaml
Engine and journal Engine, Journal, Seal engine, journal, seal
Open a file Database::open open_database
One connection per thread or domain Database::connect connect, disconnect
Run SQL query, run, exec query, run, exec
Write, retrying a lost transaction transaction transaction
Which engine may open a file resolve, inspect resolve, inspect
Close, sealing what Turso wrote close close

It also evens out the engines. The bundled SQLite in Rust turns foreign keys on by default, and the SQLite an OCaml program links does not, so one of packdir’s renames worked in one language and failed in the other until the layer set one rule. SQLite’s rollback journal, Turso’s WAL and its MVCC all answer to the same call, and Journal::Existing leaves a file’s journal alone for programs that manage their own.

The same layer now serves DNG Compare, a photography tool, whose databases stay in WAL between runs and use a marker file to say which engine owns them. That is what Seal::Wal and Journal::Existing are for.
